- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.2) mid-period, adjust forecast downward by 3–7% to reflect risk aversion.  
- For 30-day horizons, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% after a spike, assume mean reversion and reduce next period’s forecast by 2–5%.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates in early periods (e.g., first 5 days) with rising sentiment, apply a 3–5% downward bias to early forecast points.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3 or more), apply a 2–4% smoothing penalty to avoid erratic forecast swings.  
- If true outcome is below forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, assume downward momentum and reduce forecast by 1–3% per day.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is weak or neutral (0.2–0.4), apply a 1–3% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
